vulnerability.name: GO-2026-5932
vulnerability.description: golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp is unmaintained and unsafe by design

statements.impact_statement: The Caddy build verifies with go list -deps that golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp is not part of the compiled dependency graph. Trivy reports the parent x/crypto module metadata, not reachable openpgp code.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-33815
vulnerability.description: Memory-safety vulnerability (CWE-787, out-of-bounds write) in github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgproto3. Affected symbols: pgproto3.Backend.Receive, pgproto3.Bind.Decode. CVSS 9.8 CRITICAL. No upstream fix available as of 2026-04-24 (latest: v5.9.2).

statements.impact_statement: pgx/v5 is a transitive dependency pulled into the Caddy build via the smallstep/certificates module (Caddy -> smallstep/certificates -> pgx). The vulnerable code paths are pgproto3.Backend.Receive and pgproto3.Bind.Decode, which implement the PostgreSQL wire protocol (frontend/backend message parsing). These functions are only invoked when a Go application acts as a PostgreSQL server or client using the pgx driver. In this image, Caddy is used exclusively as an HTTP/HTTPS reverse proxy -- it never opens any PostgreSQL connection, does not import pgproto3, and does not call any pgx function at runtime. The application backend (NestJS/Prisma) connects to PostgreSQL via its own Node.js driver (@prisma/client), completely independent from Go/pgx. Furthermore, exploiting CVE-2026-33815 requires a malicious PostgreSQL server sending crafted wire-protocol messages to trigger the out-of-bounds write, which is impossible since Caddy has no PostgreSQL interaction whatsoever. The Caddy binary is statically compiled (CGO_ENABLED=0) with -trimpath and stripped symbols; pgx object code may be linked but is dead code never reached at runtime. We pin pgx/v5@v5.9.2 to satisfy CVE-2026-33816 and GHSA-j88v-2chj-qfwx (separate, fixed vulnerabilities). CVE-2026-33815 has no upstream fix as of v5.9.2 (GO-2026-4771: 'all versions, no known fixed'). This VEX statement will be reviewed when a fixed pgx version is released.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-84243
vulnerability.description: glibc gettext accepts LANGUAGE entries with a path and loads a message catalog from anywhere

statements.impact_statement: Exploitation needs an attacker who sets the LANGUAGE environment variable of a process and places a crafted message catalog. Every process in this image gets its environment from the container configuration chosen by the operator: runtime-init execs the entrypoint with that environment unchanged, the entrypoint only adds DATABASE_URL, and no request, upload, setting or file read at runtime writes an environment variable. The image ships no message catalog, no shell and no setuid program.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2010-4756
vulnerability.description: glibc glob() resource exhaustion through crafted patterns

statements.impact_statement: No ELF file in the image imports glob, glob64, glob_pattern_p or wordexp, the entry points of the affected glob implementation. Node, its native addons and the Prisma engines match file patterns in JavaScript or in their own code.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2018-20796
vulnerability.description: glibc POSIX regex uncontrolled recursion in check_dst_limits_calc_pos_1

statements.impact_statement: No ELF file in the image imports regcomp, regexec or the GNU re_* functions, the only entry points of the affected regex engine. Regular expressions run in V8's own engine or in the libraries' own code.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2019-1010023
vulnerability.description: glibc ldd can run code from a crafted ELF file

statements.impact_statement: The flaw is reached by running ldd on a crafted file. The distroless runtime has no ldd and no shell to run it.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2019-1010022
vulnerability.description: glibc stack protector bypass from a thread stack overflow

statements.impact_statement: The stack canary of a thread can be reached by a stack buffer overflow in that thread. This is a limit of an exploit mitigation, not a flaw an adversary can trigger: it only helps after a separate memory corruption bug in the same process, which would be a vulnerability of its own. glibc does not treat it as a security issue (sourceware bug 22850) and no release changes this behaviour.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2019-1010024
vulnerability.description: glibc ASLR weakened by the cache of thread stacks and heaps

statements.impact_statement: Reused thread stacks and heaps make their addresses easier to predict. This is a limit of an exploit mitigation, not a flaw an adversary can trigger: it only helps after a separate memory corruption bug in the same process, which would be a vulnerability of its own. glibc does not treat it as a security issue (sourceware bug 22852) and no release changes this behaviour.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2019-1010025
vulnerability.description: glibc heap addresses of new threads can be guessed

statements.impact_statement: The heap address of a new thread can be guessed from other addresses. This is a limit of an exploit mitigation, not a flaw an adversary can trigger: it only helps after a separate memory corruption bug in the same process, which would be a vulnerability of its own. glibc does not treat it as a security issue (sourceware bug 22853) and no release changes this behaviour.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-115455
vulnerability.description: libstdc++ wide-character input into std::bitset can corrupt the stack

statements.impact_statement: The affected operation is wchar_t input-stream extraction into std::bitset, implemented in the C++ <bitset> header. The final Docker stages import only libstdc++.so.6 and libgcc_s.so.1 from gcc-16 16.2.0-4, without the GCC 16 headers or compiler. Node 24.22.2 does not use wide-stream bitset extraction. The reviewed linux/amd64 runtime ELF files expose no bitset input-extraction instantiation; the bitset operation found in libvips is narrow-character output, outside this flaw. The three repositories pin identical Sharp/libvips and Argon2 amd64 artifacts. This assessment covers the shipped linux/amd64 runtime, not builder images, other architectures or arbitrary native extensions. Reassess when the Node/native dependency set or input-processing code changes. Upstream fix: https://gcc.gnu.org/cgit/gcc/commit/?id=5d419c69ce2e6b86d7da75f18736904885674219

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-114690
vulnerability.description: libstdc++ GNU parallel-mode search writes beyond its internal buffer

statements.impact_statement: The flaw is in the header-only __gnu_parallel search implementation, enabled by _GLIBCXX_PARALLEL or explicit use of the parallel headers. The Node source build enables neither mode. The reviewed linux/amd64 runtime ELF files contain no GNU parallel search symbols or OpenMP imports and have no libgomp/libomp dependency. The final stages copy only the two GCC 16 runtime libraries and cannot compile uploaded C++ code. The three repositories pin the same amd64 native artifacts. This assessment is limited to that runtime configuration; reassess for another architecture, an OpenMP/parallel-mode build or a new native addon. Upstream fix: https://gcc.gnu.org/git/?p=gcc.git;a=commit;h=c1f32b67510f6f9998deadaef5090b6663adb979

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-114691
vulnerability.description: libstdc++ std::vector<bool> constructors can overflow for element counts near SIZE_MAX

statements.impact_statement: The flaw is in the header-defined std::vector<bool> constructors, so it lives in code compiled with the affected headers, not in the runtime library itself. The final Docker stages take only libstdc++.so.6 and libgcc_s.so.1 from gcc-16 16.2.0-4, without headers or compiler. The shipped libstdc++.so.6.0.36 exports no std::vector<bool> or _Bvector symbol, and the GCC 16 runtime sources it is built from (libstdc++-v3/src and libsupc++) never use std::vector<bool>, so the vulnerable constructors are not present in what this package ships. Node, Sharp/libvips and Argon2 are compiled by their own builder toolchains and are not part of this package. Their sized vector<bool> uses reviewed in V8 take Wasm tag counts or Maglev block counts bounded far below SIZE_MAX. Reassess when the runtime libraries or the native dependency set change. Upstream fix: https://gcc.gnu.org/git/?p=gcc.git;a=commit;h=2fd8866591b5aea7098835f80ab7e176382175ae
